01 · What it makes possible

WHAT THE SKILL IS

One Claude Code skill that turns a request into a finished presentation in a look inspired by the NBG brand.

A design system in a box

  • A design system inspired by the NBG brand: 16:9 artboard, Aptos, a nine-colour teal-led palette.
  • Nine slide templates (covers, dividers, content), logos and photography bundled with the skill.
  • Guardrails written down once, applied to every deck.

A deterministic build pipeline

  • Claude authors the HTML; six zero-dependency scripts embed the images, add the editor, verify, write the rebuild script, screenshot and export.
  • A strict, browser-free gate that a deck must pass before it is delivered.
  • The PDF is printed from the deck itself, so it looks exactly like the HTML.

Decks the recipients can edit

  • Every delivered deck carries a right-click editor: fix a word, resize a card, align a row, ask an AI assistant.
  • Nothing to install: it works from a file on the desktop, in any modern browser.
  • Edits stay inside the look: the skill's fonts and palette only.

01 · What it makes possible

WHY IT MATTERS

Four problems every presentation team knows, and how the skill answers each.

Consistency

Every deck shares one look. One palette, one type stack, one artboard, one logo lockup — enforced by the skill, not by the author's memory.

The verifier rejects a deck with a fake logo, a missing photo or an external image path.

Speed

From any content to a finished deck in minutes — a brief in chat, notes, a document, a spreadsheet, an existing deck or a Google Slides draft. Once the generator exists, every re-run is one command.

Portability

One self-contained file. It can be emailed, put on a share or opened from a USB stick; it renders identically everywhere because nothing points back to the machine that built it.

Ownership

Recipients fix their own slides. A typo, a longer title, a card that should be teal, a row that needs aligning — done in place, saved as a copy, exported to PDF — without a regeneration.

Key point

The skill moves the effort from making slides look right to deciding what they should say.

5
01 · What it makes possible

WHAT YOU RECEIVE

Three files per deck, produced and verified the same way every time.

The deliverables
  • The HTML deck — 1920×1080 slides that scale to any screen, keyboard and button navigation, every logo and photo embedded, the right-click editor inlined.
  • The PDF — printed from that HTML by the browser engine: one page per slide, vector text, same colours and photography, verified page count.
  • Screenshots (on request) — one PNG per slide at 1366×768 and 1440×900, the two viewports the skill requires to check.
  • The rebuild script — deck.rebuild.mjs: run it after the skill is updated and the deck receives the newer editing tools, verified, with its PDF re-exported — no regeneration.
  • A generator for data-driven decks — a small Python script that rebuilds the deck from its content, so updates are a diff, not a redo.
What the skill asks before it starts
  • Topic, audience, slide count. The three inputs it never guesses; it asks instead.
  • Language — English by default; Greek or bilingual on request.
  • Output — HTML by default; "send as PDF" adds the export.
  • Not PowerPoint. If asked, it says so and delivers HTML and PDF — no improvised conversion.

No fallbacks: a missing input is a question to you, never a silent default.

01 · What it makes possible

THE NEWEST CAPABILITIES

What arrived most recently in the skill. Each is explained in section 02; the recipient needs no new tooling for any of them.

Edit SVG

  • A drawn icon, diagram or chart is no longer a picture: its parts — paths, shapes, text, groups — move, resize, recolour, reorder, duplicate and reword in place.
  • Path data is never rewritten; one reversible record per drawing.

One toolbar, three tabs

  • Text, Shape and SVG share one floating panel; the tab of the editor in use comes to the front by itself.
  • Pin, hide, anchor or detach it — remembered per deck.

Smarter selection

  • Shift+click takes the smallest shape under the pointer; Ctrl/Cmd+click selects everything inside a shape.
  • A compact picker at the pointer when the menu is detached; the Stack list for nested levels.

The rebuild script

  • Every deck ships with <deck>.rebuild.mjs: after a skill update it re-embeds the newer editing tools, keeps a backup, re-verifies and re-exports the PDF.
  • --check only reports.
Also

27 bundled photos with a written catalogue (Athens at dusk, data centre, network, microchip, security, developer, team analytics — three takes each); assistant settings kept per provider and an Ask about… popup on any row of the Outline or Tree; a full set of keyboard shortcuts for text, shapes, SVG parts and panels; PDFs whose shadows render correctly in macOS Preview (1.19).

02 · Ask, build, edit

INSTALLING THE SKILL

One public marketplace, two commands. No npm install, no build step: the skill is Markdown, assets and zero-dependency Node scripts.

In Claude Code
# 1 · register the marketplace (once)
/plugin marketplace add BikS2013-coding-agents/nbg-design
# 2 · install the plugin from it
/plugin install nbg-design@nbg-design
# 3 · restart Claude Code, then check
/plugin list
# later · pick up a new release
/plugin marketplace update nbg-design
claude plugin update nbg-design@nbg-design
  • The marketplace is the public repository github.com/BikS2013-coding-agents/nbg-design (branch working); its name and the plugin's name are both nbg-design, hence nbg-design@nbg-design.
  • From then on Claude uses the skill by itself whenever a presentation in this look is asked for; say nbg-design to make sure.
What lands on the machine
  • The plugin is cached under ~/.claude/plugins/cache/nbg-design/nbg-design/<version>/; the skill root is its skills/nbg-design/ folder — the <skill-root> the pipeline commands use.
  • Requirements: Node 18 or newer for the scripts. Chrome, Chromium or Edge only for screenshots and the PDF; without a browser the strict verifier is still the gate and the PDF is exported elsewhere.
  • Nothing to configure. The skill holds no credentials and reads no configuration file; assistant keys are entered by each viewer in their own browser.
  • A delivered deck outlives the install: after an update, node <deck>.rebuild.mjs re-embeds the newer editing tools — pointed at the new cache folder with --scripts or NBG_DESIGN_SCRIPTS when the recorded one is gone.

02 · Ask, build, edit

ASKING FOR A DECK

What the skill needs from you, what it decides by itself, and what it refuses to do.

It always asks for

  • Topic — what the deck is about.
  • Audience — who reads it; this sets depth and tone.
  • Slide count or depth — 8, 16, 20+.
  • Whether the bundled design-system files may be changed (they normally are not).

Approved defaults

  • Language: English. gr and bi exist; anything else must come from you.
  • Output: HTML. A PDF is always exported from the finished HTML, never authored separately.
  • Logo: shown, unless you ask to hide it.
  • Cover first, dividers between sections, content slides in between.

It will not

  • Produce or convert to PowerPoint.
  • Guess a missing input or substitute a fallback value.
  • Put an API key, token or endpoint into a deck or into the skill.
  • Reference an image by a path: every image is embedded, or the deck fails the gate.
Any content is a source

A brief typed in chat, meeting notes, a Word or Markdown document, a spreadsheet, a report, an existing HTML deck, or a Google Slides draft (read through the Slides API and rebuilt 1:1, page count kept). The skill turns whatever it is given into a cover, dividers and content slides; it only asks for what it cannot infer.

THE PIPELINE: FIVE STEPS AND ONE GATE

Claude authors; the scripts embed, add the editor and verify; a failing gate sends the deck back to the author, never forward.

12
02 · Ask, build, edit

THE PIPELINE, STEP BY STEP

What each step does and the command behind it. Steps 2 to 4 and the rebuild script are mandatory for every deck.

1

Author with tokens

Claude writes the deck on the 1920×1080 artboard, the design-system CSS and placeholders where images go: {{LOGO_PRIMARY}}, {{PHOTO_STREET}}.

2

Embed the assets

Every token becomes the verbatim base64 image. The script finds the assets next to itself, so it works from any folder and any machine.

embed-assets.mjs deck.html
3

Add the editor

One script block is inlined before </body>: the right-click menu, editing, toolbars, assistant, print. Re-running upgrades an older block.

add-deck-menu.mjs deck.html
4

Verify (strict)

Browser-free gate: no unresolved tokens, no external image paths, real logo, enough images, current menu. A failing deck is never delivered.

verify-deck.mjs deck.html --strict
5

Script, look, print

The deck's rebuild script is written next to it; screenshots per slide are read for overlaps and clipping; then the PDF is printed, one page per slide.

write-rebuild-script.mjs · screenshot-deck.mjs · export-pdf.mjs
Why tokens

Hand-pasting a 600 KB base64 photo is the step that silently fails on a headless run. Tokens make embedding a script's job, and the gate catches any slip.

THE DESIGN SYSTEM THE SKILL CARRIES

Inspired by the NBG brand and distilled into one HTML reference: nine colours, one typeface and nine templates.

Deep teal#003841primary accent, dark panels, covers
Teal#007B85secondary accent, rules, icons
Bright cyan#00ADBFhighlight accent
Electric cyan#00CFE7highlight, sparingly
Black#0A1416body text on light
Grey 1#BEC1BErules, muted surfaces
Grey 2#939793secondary text
Cream#F5F8F6light page background
White#FFFFFFtext on dark, cards on cream

Format & type

16:9, 1920×1080 artboard, scaled to fit any viewport. Aptos for everything, with a system fallback where it is absent — the stack is never swapped.

Nine templates

Covers (hero photo, image card, alternate), dividers (photo, deep teal, bright), content (image right, two columns, stat-led). Content pages stay calm and mostly monochrome; accent blocks belong to covers and openers.

Eight assets

Three logo lockups — primary for light backgrounds, knockout for dark, small for footers — and five photographs, each shipped with a ready-made data URI. The logo is always the image, never text or a box.

02 · Ask, build, edit

QUALITY GATES

What must be true before a deck leaves. The first gate runs anywhere; the others need a browser.

verify-deck --strict (browser-free, mandatory)
  • No unresolved tokens and no image referenced by file://, absolute, relative or http path — every image is a data: URI.
  • Enough embedded images (default 2) and a minimum size (200 KB): a photo-less deck is the classic tell of a skipped step.
  • A real logo: bare “NBG” text nodes that could stand in for the lockup fail the gate.
  • The current editor block: missing, PDF-only or older than the skill's — fail or warn; incomplete — always fail.
Visual and print checks
  • Fit: the full slide visible at 1366×768 and 1440×900 with no scrolling caused by the artboard.
  • No collisions: title, body, card rows, callouts, footer and page number keep separate zones — at least 32 px between groups and 72 px above the footer. Crowded content is cut or split, never squeezed or hidden.
  • PDF = deck: page count equals slide count and every slide box equals the page box, or the exporter exits with an error.
  • Read the pictures: screenshots and rasterised PDF pages are inspected, not just produced.

EDITING 2 · TEXT

Double-click any text. The whole block becomes editable in place, with a teal outline; the slide's CSS is never touched.

⋮⋮⚓⧉
TextShapeSVG
⋮⋮BIUSA−24 pxA+Aptos ▾Colour≡☰≡ClearDone
Editing
  • Double-click a text (or right-click → Edit text). Type, Backspace, Shift+Enter for a line break, Ctrl/Cmd+Z to undo.
  • Enter or a click outside applies; Esc cancels. Deck shortcuts (arrows, space) are paused while you edit.
  • Paste and drop insert plain text. Anything a browser wraps around typed text is unwrapped when the edit is applied, so no stray formatting leaks in.
  • Accent spans inside a title (the teal word in a heading) stay intact.
The formatting row
  • Selection first. Every control applies to the selected run when there is one, and to the whole block when there is none.
  • B / I / U / S (Ctrl/Cmd+B I U), A− / A+ or an exact px size (Ctrl/Cmd+Shift+> / <), font from the design-system stacks, colour from the skill's palette only, alignment for the block.
  • Clear removes the selection's formatting, or returns the block to its authored style. Done applies.
  • Fonts and colours are limited on purpose: a viewer can fix a slide but cannot leave the look.

EDITING 3 · SHAPES

Right-click a card, photo panel, image or text block → Resize / move shape. A teal frame with eight handles appears.

⋮⋮⚓⧉
TextShapeSVG
⋮⋮X120Y300W420H300FillTransparent ▾Border1 px ▾Radius8Opacity100ShadowSoft ▾Stack ▾ResetDone
⋮⋮OrderFrontForwardBackwardBackAlign⇤⇹⇥⤒⇳⤓Distribute↔↕to selection ▾GroupUngroup</>
Moving and resizing
  • Drag a handle to resize (Shift keeps the proportions), drag inside to move. Arrow keys nudge by 1 px, Shift by 10; Alt+arrows resize.
  • Tab selects the enclosing shape, Shift+Tab steps back in; Esc, Enter or a click outside finishes.
  • Only inline geometry changes — left, top, width, height — and pointer movement is divided by the slide's current scale, so coordinates stay exact artboard pixels at any window size.
  • Elements in normal flow get only the right and bottom handles: they grow right and down. Reset restores size, position and style.
The shape row
  • X / Y / W / H typed exactly; fill (the palette, transparent or default); border none to 6 px in a palette colour; corner radius, opacity, shadow none / soft / strong.
  • Everything is inline style on the element, recorded as one reversible edit per element.
  • Neighbours do not re-flow. Widen one card in a row, then use Distribute or move the next card to restore the spacing. The overlap rules still apply to the result.
  • Stack lists the enclosing shapes, the selected one and its children, for the level a click cannot reach.
  • Edit SVG: a drawn icon, diagram or chart has parts of its own — the next two slides. The SVG as a whole is still a shape: Resize / move shape sizes and places it.

EDITING 4 · EDIT SVG: THE PARTS OF A DRAWING

Right-click a drawn icon, diagram or chart → Edit SVG. The drawing gets a dashed outline and every part inside it becomes a thing you can pick.

Entering and selecting
  • Three ways in: right-click the drawing → Edit SVG; double-click a drawing that is already selected as a shape; click one of its parts in the Tree tab.
  • What a part is: a path, rect, circle, ellipse, line, polygon, text, image, use reference or group. Nothing inside defs, clip paths, masks or symbols.
  • A click picks the innermost part under the pointer — through the frame of a selected group too, so its members are one click away. Shift+click adds a part (or removes a selected one); Ctrl/Cmd+click selects what is inside the part there; Ctrl/Cmd+A or All every top-level part.
  • Tab selects the enclosing group, Shift+Tab the first part inside; the Parts list offers every part in drawing order.
Moving, resizing, styling
  • The selection gets a frame with eight handles — several parts: one frame spanning them, a dashed mark per part. Drag inside to move, a handle to resize (Shift keeps proportions); arrows nudge by one SVG unit, Shift ten, Alt+arrows resize — all selected parts together, keeping their places.
  • The SVG row: X / Y / W / H in the drawing's own units; fill and stroke from the palette, None or Default; stroke width; opacity; the text of a label (one run; Enter applies).
  • Order in the drawing (Ctrl/Cmd+] / [), Duplicate (Ctrl/Cmd+D; copies sit on the originals), Delete (Delete), Reset SVG (every part as designed), Done.
  • Esc deselects the part, then ends the session; Enter, Done, Finish SVG editing in the menu or a click outside the drawing end it too.

02 · Ask, build, edit

EDITING 5 · WHAT AN SVG EDIT WRITES

Geometry goes into attributes, colour into presentation attributes, and the whole drawing becomes one reversible record. The path data itself is never touched.

Geometry, never path data

  • A move or resize is written in the part's parent coordinate system: the screen box is mapped back through the parent's transform.
  • A rect or image without a transform gets plain x / y / width / height; a pure move of text, a use, a circle, an ellipse or a line changes x / y, cx / cy or x1…y2.
  • Everything else — a path, a scaled text, a group — gets a matrix() prepended to its own transform. The d attribute stays as drawn.

Colours, order, text

  • Fill, stroke, stroke width and opacity become presentation attributes, or the inline style property when the part already sets one — so the change wins over the stylesheet without touching it.
  • Order is a real move in the drawing order inside the parent; Duplicate clones without ids and places the copy after the original.
  • The text field replaces the one run of a <text>; labels with several runs are edited as source in the Tree tab.

One record for the whole drawing

  • Every operation records the <svg> element's inner HTML as a single html edit — the same kind as a text edit — so it persists in the browser, lands in the saved copy, is discarded per slide and prints.
  • Reset SVG drops that record. Sessions are exclusive: editing text, selecting a shape or preparing a print ends the SVG session first.
  • SVG text is never contenteditable; the SVG as a whole is still a shape for Resize / move shape.
Known limits

The frame is the axis-aligned screen box: a part inside a rotated group is moved correctly in that group's space, but its frame does not rotate. Parts sized in percentages or with a CSS transform take the matrix path. The five diagrams in this deck are editable this way.

02 · Ask, build, edit

EDITING 6 · SEVERAL SHAPES AT ONCE

Text blocks, cards, panels and images alike. The frame spans the selection and each member gets a dashed mark.

Selecting

  • Shift+click adds the smallest shape under the pointer, or removes it when it is already selected.
  • Shift+drag on the slide draws a box: every top-level shape fully inside is added.
  • Ctrl/Cmd+A selects every top-level shape of the slide; Ctrl/Cmd+click selects everything inside the shape under the pointer; a shape with nothing inside is picked alone, even a group member, and on the same spot again cycles outward.
  • The menu offers Add to / Remove from selection / Select all shapes; the Outline tab does it with checkboxes.

Arranging

  • Order: bring to front / forward, send backward / to back (Ctrl/Cmd+] and [, Shift for front / back).
  • Align left, centre, right, top, middle, bottom — relative to the selection's own box or to the slide.
  • Distribute horizontally or vertically with equal gaps; the first and last stay put.
  • Dragging moves all, handles scale all proportionally, every style control applies to all.

Grouping

  • Group (Ctrl/Cmd+G) / Ungroup (Ctrl/Cmd+Shift+G).
  • A group is logical: members carry a data-nbg-group mark and always select, move, resize, align and order together.
  • Groups persist in the browser, land in the saved copy and are removed by Discard edits.
  • The page structure is never rebuilt: ordering is an inline z-index, grouping an attribute, so every earlier edit stays valid.
Nested shapes

A click lands on one level only. Use Select at this point in the menu (front-most first, containers, shapes behind), the toolbar's Stack list, or Tab / Shift+Tab to reach the others.

02 · Ask, build, edit

EDITING 7 · STRUCTURE, WINDOWS AND THE PICKER

The Outline and Tree tabs, panels that leave the browser window, and the compact menu that takes over while the big one is away.

Outline & Tree

  • Outline: the slide's shapes nested by containment — cards, text blocks, images — with kind icons, sizes, group badges, a text filter, checkboxes, All / None. Click a name to select it, Shift+click adds.
  • Tree: the slide's HTML elements, synced both ways with the selection; double-click edits a text; hovering outlines the element on the slide.
  • Under the tree, the selected element's editable source behind a draggable splitter. Apply records it like any other edit; scripts are stripped. For people who know what they are doing.

Detachable panels

  • ⧉ on the menu (structure and assistant included) or on the toolbar moves it into a window of its own: a Document Picture-in-Picture window in Chrome and Edge — always on top, no browser chrome, anywhere on the desktop, even off the browser — or a pop-up elsewhere.
  • The panel keeps working on the deck from there; closing the window, ✕ or Esc brings it back.
  • A detached panel is pinned: it idles rather than disappears when nothing is selected. Screenshots asked from a detached assistant use that window's permission.

The picker

  • While the menu is detached, or open on a panel tab, a right-click on the slide opens a compact picker at the pointer instead of the full menu.
  • It holds the same Select at this point hierarchy — front-most first, containers and shapes behind — plus Edit text.
  • A click selects, Shift+click adds, Esc closes it. The big menu keeps its place and its tab.
  • Ctrl/Cmd+Shift+O / H open Outline / Tree directly; Ctrl/Cmd+Shift+L the assistant.

  • The editor in use takes the front. Text being edited, or a selection made only of text blocks → Text; any other selection → Shape; a drawing in SVG editing → SVG. The panel appears with the selection and follows it.

02 · Ask, build, edit

EDITING 10 · ASK THE ASSISTANT

An AI request from inside the deck, with the slide as context. The viewer brings their own endpoint and key; nothing is baked in.

Ask

  • A prompt from the drop-down: Free request, Review the slide, Proofread the text, Tighten the copy, Speaker notes, Restyle the selection, Rewrite the selection's text, plus your own.
  • A request box for extra instructions.

Attach

  • Screenshot of the slide (tab capture; toolbars hidden, cropped to the slide).
  • Slide source — its HTML plus the CSS rules it uses; embedded images travel as small placeholders, so photos cost no tokens.
  • Selected element source.
  • Clipboard image — paste, drop or Read clipboard.

Reply

  • Show the answer in the panel, with Copy and Apply to selection.
  • Replace the selected element: the reply is the element's replacement HTML — same tag, scripts stripped, recorded as a normal edit — with Undo.
  • Right-click a row in Outline or Tree for an Ask about… popup on that element.

Settings

  • Providers: Anthropic, Azure-hosted Anthropic (Microsoft Foundry), OpenAI-compatible, Azure OpenAI, DeepSeek.
  • Endpoint, model or deployment, API key (kept in this browser, or for the tab only), Test.
  • Settings are kept per provider; nothing is defaulted — a missing value blocks the request with a message.
  • The page calls the endpoint directly; a provider that blocks browser calls needs a gateway.
Privacy

Each attachment is a checkbox, so the viewer decides per request what leaves the machine. The key never enters the deck file or a saved copy.

02 · Ask, build, edit

EDITING 11 · KEEPING, SHARING AND PRINTING YOUR CHANGES

The deck on disk never changes by itself. Edits live in the browser until you save a copy.

  • Edits persist in the browser, keyed by the file: reload the deck and they are still there. They exist only in that browser — the original file is untouched.
  • Save edited copy downloads <name>-edited.html: your edits applied to a pristine snapshot of the deck taken at load. The copy is still one self-contained file and carries the editor itself.
  • Discard changes on this slide restores the slide under the pointer (the hint counts its changes); Discard edits restores every slide.
  • Refresh the tools later: node deck.rebuild.mjs replaces only the editor block with the one the skill ships now, keeps a backup, re-runs the strict gate and re-exports the PDF. --check only reports CURRENT or REBUILD NEEDED.
  • Export to PDF applies the same print layout as the command-line exporter and opens the print dialog: choose Save as PDF in Chrome or Edge. Page size, zero margins and backgrounds are preset — one page per slide, the same layout as the CLI export. Blurred shadows are printed as images on this path (block v13), so the PDF also renders correctly in macOS Preview.
What the editor can and cannot do
In the deck, by anyoneBy regenerating, with the skill
Text, formatting, size, font, palette colour, alignmentNew images or photos
Geometry and style of shapes: fill, border, radius, opacity, shadowNew elements, new slides, new layouts
Order, alignment, distribution, groups of several shapesStructural changes to the page
AI-assisted rewrites and restyles of an elementAnything outside the skill's fonts and palette

A PDF of an edited deck is printed from the saved copy — the CLI prints what is on disk.

ANATOMY OF THE SKILL FOLDER

15 MB, 14 of them photography; one Markdown file that is the whole behaviour, seven scripts, five libraries, and the design system with its assets.

nbg-design/plugin nbg-design v1.19.0 · marketplace BikS2013-coding-agents/nbg-design · MIT

  • SKILL.md is the contract. Inputs, defaults, palette, templates, embedding rules, the editor's behaviour, the PDF rules and the quality checklist — all in one file, no separate configuration.
  • Everything resolves relative to the skill root, never to the working directory: the scripts find the assets next to themselves, so the skill works from any folder, on any machine, through a symlink.
  • Installed as a project skill via a symlink in .claude/skills/ pointing at the plugin checkout, so the working tree is the live skill.
  • References are history, not behaviour: every design decision from v1.3 to v1.19 is recorded with its rationale, mechanism and verification in project-design.md.

03 · Make it your own

INSIDE A DELIVERED DECK

One HTML file carries the slides and the editor; the browser keeps the edits; three ways lead out.

33
03 · Make it your own

INSIDE THE EDITOR

How a standalone file:// deck can be edited, remembered and handed back without ever writing to itself.

Edit records

  • Every change is a record {{ path, original, … }} where path is the child-index path from the root — cheap, exact, and the reason the DOM is never restructured.
  • Three kinds: html (text and selection-level formatting), style (block formatting, geometry, fill, border, z-index), group (the data-nbg-group attribute). An SVG session records the whole <svg> as one html record.
  • Stored in localStorage under nbg-deck-edits:<path>#<title>; re-applied on load; a record whose original no longer matches is dropped.

Pristine snapshot

  • When the inlined script runs — after the deck's own scripts, before any runtime element and before stored edits — it takes an outerHTML snapshot.
  • Save edited copy parses that snapshot with DOMParser, applies the records, and downloads the result: it loads exactly like the original and carries the menu.
  • The print path uses the same print-layout shim as the CLI, then restores every class, style and attribute it touched.

Geometry, order, groups

  • A "shape" is a positioned element, one with a background, border or shadow, or an image; otherwise the text block.
  • Pointer deltas are divided by the slide's scale (rect.width / offsetWidth), so coordinates are artboard pixels.
  • Ordering ranks siblings by effective layer and writes an inline z-index; a negative index makes the parent a stacking context with isolation: isolate.
  • Rich contenteditable, not plaintext-only, because the latter forces pre-wrap and re-flows titles.
Design rule

Inline style and attributes only, never DOM re-ordering — so every earlier record's path stays valid and every change stays reversible.

34
03 · Make it your own

THE PDF PATH

The PDF is the deck, printed by the same engine that renders it. Nothing is re-laid out for paper.

What the exporter does
  • Opens the deck in headless Chrome, Chromium or Edge over the DevTools pipe — nothing to install.
  • Lifts the host layer only: navigation toggles (.active, .hidden, inline display), the viewport-fit wrappers and scaling, buttons and counters; jumps animations to their end state; forces print-color-adjust: exact.
  • Makes every top-level .slide visible in flow and prints with Page.printToPDF: page size = the measured slide box (1920×1080 px = 20 × 11.25 in), zero margins, backgrounds on, scale 1.
  • Verifies: page count equals slide count and every slide box equals the page box; otherwise exit 1 (the PDF is still written for diagnosis). Exit 3 means no browser on the host.
  • Re-anchors the soft masks (since 1.19): Chrome writes every blurred shadow as a luminosity mask that macOS Preview mis-positions into gray blocks. The exporter rewrites them to page space as an incremental update; every other viewer draws the same picture. fix-pdf-soft-masks.mjs does it for older PDFs.
Rules that are not negotiable
  • Aesthetics are frozen. No print stylesheets, no resized slides, no font swaps "to make it print". A mismatch is a bug in the deck, fixed in the HTML.
  • No fakes. No window.print() at A4, no browser Save-as-PDF with headers and margins, no office round-trips, no stitched screenshots.
  • Every top-level slide carries the slide class — the exporter and the screenshot helper key on it.
  • Fonts come from the exporting host: with Aptos absent, PDF and screenshots share the same fallback. Export where Aptos is installed if it must appear.
  • Never print a deck that fails verify-deck --strict. The in-deck Export to PDF inlines the very same shim; since the print dialog's PDF cannot be post-processed, that path prints blurred shadows as images instead (block v13).
35
03 · Make it your own

THE CONFIGURATION HOOK: ONE EDITOR FOR ANY HTML PAGE

Since v1.15 the editor is configured, not forked. A deck keeps its defaults; any other document declares what its editable regions are.

window.nbgDeckMenuConfig
window.nbgDeckMenuConfig = {
  mode: 'deck' | 'page',print: one page per slide, or the browser's pagination
  root: '.slide',CSS selector of the editable regions (top-level matches)
  unit: 'Slide',the word the UI uses: Slide, Page, Section …
  title: '…',the label in the menu header
  aiSystem: '…'replaces the assistant's system prompt
};
  • Written as the block's first statement by addMenu(html, config) / buildMenuBlock(config); readMenuConfig(html) reads it back. The CLI has no flags: a deck always gets the defaults.
  • Page mode: the print path adds only background and animation rules; wording says page / Section N; the assistant gets page-oriented prompts (Review the page, Summarise the page …).
Reusing the skill in generators
  • A deck can be a data-driven Python generator: a helper section (icons, header, footer, pills, numbered circles) and one add() per slide, sharing one deck.css and deck.js with sibling decks.
  • Slides can be sliced out of another generator by comment markers and re-executed, so a slide reused across decks is one line.
  • A rebuild.sh per deck detects skill, generator or asset changes, builds the next version through the five steps and refreshes a fixed-name -latest copy — the stable link.
  • This deck was built that way: a 550-line generator, the shared CSS plus 150 lines of additions, and the pipeline.
36
03 · Make it your own

RULES THAT KEEP IT SAFE

The constraints written into SKILL.md that every generated deck, and every future change to the skill, must respect.

Delivery

  • Run order: author → embed → add menu → verify strict → rebuild script → screenshots → PDF. Never deliver a deck that fails the gate.
  • Every image a data: URI; the logo always the bundled lockup.
  • Fit at 1366×768 and 1440×900; no element collisions; 32 px between groups, 72 px above the footer.
  • PDF only from the verified HTML, only through the exporter.

Secrets & fallbacks

  • The skill holds no credentials. Assistant keys are the viewer's and live only in their browser — never in the skill, a deck or a saved copy.
  • No fallback values: a missing input is a question, a missing setting a message. Exceptions are written into the project memory first.
  • The agent never enters endpoints or keys for a recipient and never relies on the assistant for its own work.

Scope

  • The look cannot be left from the editor: fonts limited to the design-system stacks, colours to the NBG-inspired palette. The Tree tab's source editor is the one deliberate exception, for experts.
  • The editor changes text, formatting, geometry, order, groups and shape style. Images, new elements and structure are the skill's job — regenerate.
  • PowerPoint is out of scope; newsletters, GPT and NotebookLM artifacts of the original project are excluded unless asked for.

Summary

USING IT TOMORROW

One line for recipients, six commands for builders, one marketplace to install from.

Tell the recipient

Double-click any text to edit it (Enter applies, Esc cancels). Right-click for Resize / move shape (Shift+click or Shift+drag selects several; the toolbar orders, aligns, distributes and groups them), Edit SVG (the parts of a drawn icon, diagram or chart; one toolbar with Text, Shape and SVG tabs serves all three), Ask the assistant, Export to PDF and Save edited copy. After a skill update, node deck.rebuild.mjs refreshes the editing tools and the PDF.

Where it lives
  • Public marketplace github.com/BikS2013-coding-agents/nbg-design: /plugin marketplace add BikS2013-coding-agents/nbg-design, then /plugin install nbg-design@nbg-design.
  • This deck: github.com/BikS2013-presentations/deck-work-nbgdesign, browsable on GitHub Pages and always current as deck/NBG-Design-Skill-Explained-latest.html; its generator and rebuild.sh live in the same repository.
